one_liner: Memory-safe Rust port of the Ada WHATWG URL parser; 7.4% faster than C++ Ada on a 9-URL corpus.
what_it_does: Parses, normalizes and edits URLs per the WHATWG URL Standard, with UTS #46 IDNA, URLSearchParams and optional URLPattern, and the library forbids unsafe code. Its `Url` copies Ada's `url_aggregator` design: one normalized `String` plus eight `u32` offsets. Getters such as `href()`, `hostname()` and `pathname()` return slices of that buffer without allocating, and setters leave the URL unchanged if they fail. The API looks like the `ada-url` Rust wrapper but is not the same: `Url::parse` takes an already-parsed `Option<&Url>` base (`parse_with_base` takes a string), errors are `ada_rs::ParseError`, and Ada's C ABI and multi-string `ada::url` type are not ported.
how_it_is_fast: Conservative validate-and-copy fast paths. For http(s) URLs that are already normalized, it finds delimiters with `memchr`/`memchr2`/`memchr3` (runtime-dispatched SIMD) and checks host bytes against a 256-entry const lookup table. It then copies the input into one `String` with a single allocation and records the offsets, lowercasing the host or inserting a missing `/` only when needed. More hand-written paths cover normalized file URLs, common authority URLs (credentials, ports, IPv4/IPv6, IDNA hosts via the `idna` crate), opaque URLs and simple relative references. Every other input goes to Servo's `url` crate, and ada-rs patches the result to match Ada's output, so the speedup only applies to inputs that hit a fast path.
when_to_use: Pure-Rust services or tools that parse many URLs which are already normalized http(s) (logs, crawlers, proxies, analytics). This is the subset where it measured 21.7% faster than C++ Ada.
Codebases whose memory-safety policy rules out linking C++ Ada through FFI, but where Servo `url` is too slow (37.5% slower than ada-rs on the same 9-URL corpus).

Rust code that needs serialization matching Node.js/Ada. It passes the pinned WPT, Ada-extra, IDNA and setter fixtures, and differential tests compare 10,000 generated URLs and 5,000 SearchParams mutation sequences against C++ Ada.
Read-heavy use: parse once, then read components many times. Getters are checked slices of one buffer and do not allocate.
when_not_to_use: Setter-heavy workloads. Nine setters (protocol, username, password, host, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash) re-parse the whole href with Servo `url` and then rebuild the `Url`. No setter benchmarks are published.

Workloads full of unusual, relative or non-normalized inputs. On the full WPT fixture it is at parity with C++ Ada (0.6% faster overall, 0.4% slower with no base), and inputs that miss the fast paths run at roughly Servo `url` speed plus a copy.
C or C++ projects: there is no C ABI, so use Ada directly.
Production dependencies that need maturity: v0.1.0, two commits on one day (2026-07-28), one author, 0 stars, and not published on crates.io (git dependency only).
Small dependency trees: it wraps Servo `url` rather than replacing it, and also pulls in `idna`, `percent-encoding` and `memchr`, plus `urlpattern` if you enable URLPattern.

integration.form: crate (v0.1.0; not on crates.io, use a git dependency)
integration.dependencies: memchr 2.8, idna 1.1, percent-encoding 2.3, url 2.5.8 (Servo; default features off; used as the fallback parser and for form_urlencoded); optional: serde, urlpattern 0.6 (`url-pattern` feature), ada-url 4.0.0 (`bench-ada` feature, builds C++ Ada for tests and benches only)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024. Cargo.toml declares rust-version 1.85, but the library uses let-chains, which became stable in Rust 1.88, so 1.88+ in practice.
integration.platforms: Any Rust target with std. CI runs tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows (stable) plus Miri. memchr's SIMD dispatch covers x86-64, AArch64 and WebAssembly. Benchmarks were run only on an Apple M5 Pro (arm64).
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. `Url` is plain owned data (a `String`, integer offsets and small enums; it implements `Clone`) with no interior mutability. The length limit is a process-wide `AtomicU32`, so `set_max_input_length` affects all threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — Rust only. Method names follow the ada-url wrapper (href, hostname, set_*, can_parse, UrlSearchParams), but `Url::parse` takes an `Option<&Url>` base instead of `Option<&str>` and the error types differ. There is no C/C++ API, so it cannot replace C++ Ada itself.

gotchas: It is a hybrid, not a full native port. ARCHITECTURE.md calls the Servo `url` fallback a 'correctness bridge' for states not yet handled natively. After the fallback, ada-rs fixes drive letters, file localhost, trailing spaces in opaque paths and `^` in paths so the output matches Ada.

The WPT benchmark treats the two parsers differently. benches/wpt.rs gives ada-rs an already-parsed `&Url` base, but gives C++ Ada the base as a string, and `ada_parse_with_base` parses that base again inside the C API. Each C++ Ada call also goes through the C ABI and heap-allocates an `ada::result` wrapper. Both effects favor ada-rs in the with-base, all-cases and invalid-case numbers.
`url.search_params()` returns a detached copy. Call `url.set_search_params(&params)` to apply changes; unlike JavaScript's `URL.searchParams`, the two are not kept in sync.
`set_max_input_length` is global and uses a Relaxed atomic. The default is u32::MAX (no limit).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ada-rs over Ada (C++) when you work in Rust and want Ada-compatible output with no C++ toolchain or FFI; stay with Ada for C/C++ code, for production maturity, or for setter-heavy code. Compared with sorug (Rust, benchmarked only against Servo url) and lucid-url (mixed results against Ada), ada-rs is the one with a head-to-head benchmark and differential tests against C++ Ada, but its measured wins are small and mostly on normalized URLs.
verified_claims_summary: Divan medians for parse plus href on an Apple M5 Pro (macOS 26.5, arm64), Rust 1.97.1 / LLVM 22.1.8 with fat LTO: 1.041 µs vs 1.124 µs for C++ Ada 4.0.0 (called through the ada-url Rust wrapper) over 9 URLs, 244 ns vs 312 ns on the 5 normalized ones, a tie on the 4 complex ones, and 1.666 µs for Servo url. On all 891 WPT cases it is 0.6% faster overall (26.2% faster on invalid inputs, 0.4% slower with no base); the C++ compiler used to build Ada is not named.
status_note: New rather than proven: two commits on 2026-07-28 with green CI (Linux, macOS, Windows, Miri), v0.1.0, not on crates.io, 0 stars. It is dual MIT/Apache-2.0 and about 4,000 lines of safe Rust, so it is small enough to vendor, but treat it as an experiment.
